national.title: Harmeet Dhillon, DOJ's controversial civil rights chief, resigns
national.summary: Harmeet Dhillon, the assistant attorney general for the Civil Rights Division, resigned from the Justice Department on Thursday.

"She has defended the civil liberties of every American and enforced the law without fear or favor. The Department is grateful for her dedicated public service, and we wish her every success in her future endeavors."Dhillon oversaw a mass exodus from the Civil Rights Division last year, with more than 75% of its staff departing. national.title: Paraguay President Santiago Peña resigns after bank collapse
national.summary: The move follows a bank collapse and after the lower house of congress voted in favour of pursuing an impeachment trial against him.
national.body:
Paraguay's President Santiago Peña has announced his resignation following a political crisis sparked by the collapse of a bank linked to him.

"I want to apologise to the people if at any point I failed," he said in a video message on social media. "It was never my intention to betray the trust you placed in me."

The crisis erupted after Ueno Bank entered an insolvency process, which froze all operations. Lawmakers accused Peña, who was a shareholder until last year in the company that owned the bank, of conflicts of interest and misconduct.

Peña has rejected suggestions of impropriety. His resignation comes after Paraguay's lower house of congress voted in favour of pursuing an impeachment trial.

In his video message posted on X, Peña said his resignation was to protect stability, social peace and democratic institutions.

Ueno Bank has said it has about three million customers, equivalent to about 60% of Paraguay's adult population.

It held pensions and some other public funds and, after its collapse earlier this week, millions could not access their accounts.

The central bank seized the digital lender, and people took to the streets protesting and demanding Peña's resignation.

national.title: Mississippi Senate race is toss-up, with razor-thin margin
national.summary: The Senate race in deep-red Mississippi remains unresolved Thursday morning, as Democrat Scott Colom has mounted a surprisingly competitive challenge to incumbent Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith.
national.body: Washington — The Senate midterm race in deep-red Mississippi remains unresolved, with Democrat Scott Colom mounting a surprisingly competitive challenge to incumbent GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith. With about 96% of the vote in, at one point Wednesday morning just a few dozen votes separated the candidates, a stunningly close result in the Magnolia State. By midday Thursday, Colom was leading Hyde-Smith by just over 1,700 votes. Hyde-Smith, 67, has been in the Senate since 2018 and is seeking reelection. But Colom, a district attorney, launched a formidable challenge, and could deliver Democrats yet another victory. Democrats saw a slew of wins in Senate races Tuesday night, including in states that President Trump won by double digits in the 2024 elections. With more than four flips of GOP-held seats, Democrats secured enough seats to take control of the chamber in the new year. If Colom manages to pull off a victory, he would add to their majority. Colom, 43, is a seventh-generation Mississippian who campaigned on cost of living and health care issues. Democrats began investing in the race in recent weeks, seeing an opportunity for a pickup. But the possible outcome still appeared exceedingly unlikely heading into Election Day.Mr. Trump won Mississippi by 20 points in 2024, and the state hasn't elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1982. Speaking to supporters in the wee hours of the morning on Wednesday, Colom said, "The results are all trending in our direction.""We are trending in counties that people thought we had no chance to compete in," Colom said. "And we're winning them."The unresolved race in Mississippi comes as Alaska's Senate race is also outstanding, leaving the size of Democrats' majority up in the air.

national.title: Peanut allergy study finds babies should be retested. Here's what to know.
national.summary: About one in 50 kids in the United States has a peanut allergy​. But a new study from Australia shows parents should consider having their kids retested.
national.body: It's one of the most common hardships for parents with young kids â policing what their children eat when they are diagnosed with a peanut allergy. About one in 50 kids in the United States has a peanut allergy. But a new study from Australia shows parents should consider having their kids retested.More than one-third of babies thought to have a peanut allergy could safely have the diagnosis removed, according to research from the Murdoch Children's Research Institute and the National Allergy Centre of Excellence, published this week in The Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology. Infants in the study had recently had a reaction to peanuts and then tested positive for a peanut allergy. However, 34.8% of those infants who tested positive were then found not to have an allergic reaction when given slowly increasing doses of peanuts under strict medical supervision, according to the study.Oral food challenges aren't being used enough, according to those who conducted the study, as most parents rely on testing alone."Oral food challenges are not currently used routinely for every infant with suspected peanut allergy," National Allergy Centre of Excellence Director Kirsten Perrett said in a statement. "But our results show that clinical history and allergy testing alone were not enough to accurately diagnose peanut allergy in many cases. A supervised oral food challenge should be routinely considered to confirm the diagnosis before an infant starts oral immunotherapy."Those who did not have an adverse reaction during the oral food challenge were considered peanut tolerant and had their allergy label removed, according to the study.But parents should never attempt doing a similar challenge on their own, experts warn."If you have an infant that was diagnosed with a peanut allergy, it may make sense to have a conversation with your allergist about ... an oral food challenge," CBS News medical contributor and immunologist Dr. Tania Elliott told "CBS Mornings." "This is not something to try at home â 12% of those babies had anaphylaxis. OK, so this needs to happen in a monitored setting in the doctor's office, where they're given small amounts of peanut to determine if they're still allergic.""And all children should be retested, even if they have allergies, every year to determine whether or not they still have the allergy," Elliott added.

national.title: 3 injured in shooting at Des Moines, Iowa, post office
national.summary: A suspect was in custody in Des Moines, Iowa, after two people were shot at the city's main post office and a third was injured trying to escape, authorities said.
national.body: A suspect was in custody in Des Moines, Iowa, on Thursday after two people were shot at the city's main post office and a third was injured trying to escape, authorities said. None of the injuries were believed to be life-threatening, police said. "They're all at the hospital; they are being cared for right now," Sgt. Paul Parizek said of the victims. Parizek said officers responded within three minutes. The shooting happened on the second floor of the post office and reports started coming in of shots fired around 9:10 a.m. local time.Parizek said the suspect is a woman at the postal facility. She has not yet been publicly identified. CBS affiliate KCCI-TV posted video of officers swarming the scene after the shooting. The main post office is just north of downtown Des Moines and across the street from one of the city's main hospitals. The building is a four-story regional sorting facility with a walk-in service counter accessible to the public. The Associated Press has several phone calls out seeking more information. Gov. Kim Reynolds said she's in contact with the Department of Public Safety regarding the shooting. "The suspected shooter is in custody and the investigation is ongoing," she posted online. "We are monitoring the situation and our prayers are with everyone involved. Grateful for the immediate response by law enforcement." Des Moines Public Schools said in a social media post that after being notified by police at 9:20 a.m. of the shooting at the post office, the district's nearby elementary school, welcome center and nutrition center went into a secure status, meaning no one was allowed in or out of the buildings. The district said the secure status was lifted after police notified them at 10 a.m. that a suspect was in custody. Sen. Chuck Grassley posted on X: "Im following news of the shooting this morning at the Main Post Office in Des Moines Gr8ful to law enforcement + first responders who acted quickly 2 detain the shooter + treat the injured Barbara & I are praying for all those impacted."

national.body:

JUNEAU, Alaska (AP) — Alaskans settled in Wednesday to await more results from key races on the general election ballot, including a bitterly fought U.S. Senate campaign and an open seat for governor.

A ballot measure seeking to repeal Alaska's unique system of open primaries and ranked vote general elections also was too early to call.

If no candidate wins more than 50% of first-choice votes, rankings will come into play. Alaska accepts ballots from overseas voters for up to 15 days after the election, making Nov. 18 the date targeted by state elections officials to tabulate under the ranked vote system.

The major candidates in the Senate race are two-term Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan and Democratic former Rep. Mary Peltola.

national.summary: At least 20 flights in Europe deal with bomb threats, adding to what one expert calls an unusual level of hoaxes in a short time period, suggesting "a very deliberate act."
national.body: Paris — At least 20 commercial flights in Europe had to deal with bomb threats Thursday, with at least one being diverted to a military base in France. While authorities have reported no explosives discovered on any of the jets, and they all appeared to be hoaxes, Thursday's incidents add to a fast-growing number of journeys hit by similar threats this week, which one expert said suggested a "very deliberate act." British authorities dismissed threats to about seven flights earlier this week as hoaxes, but the number of impacted journeys soared to at least 27 on Thursday, meaning significant disruption for thousands of passengers and raising concerns about a possible coordinated effort to impact travel on the continent. So far, it remains unclear who, if anyone, is behind any such coordinated action, and no authorities have confirmed a link between any of the threats.David Kaminski-Morrow, Air Transport Editor with FlightGlobal, declined to speculate on who might be behind the threats this week, but he noted that "we currently live in a time of political aggression in regions including Europe, and it's a pretty effective tactic if someone is looking to cause disruption.""The cluster of threats seems unusual, but it's hard to determine the extent to which they might be organized," he said, noting that "the publicity alone could spur further threats unrelated to earlier ones."Kaminski-Morrow noted that, under an international aviation convention in place for more than 80 years, the pilot in command of a flight has the final authority over its safety, "and airlines always take threats to safety seriously. national.title: McDonald's plans to cook up new affordable menu bundles
national.summary: McDonald's CEO Christopher Kempczinski said the company is testing new value pairings at select U.S. locations.
national.body: McDonald's is testing new affordable menu bundles as it works to attract inflation-weary customers struggling with the cost of living. McDonald's CEO Christopher Kempczinski said Wednesday during a call with Wall Street analysts that the fast-food chain recently launched an eight-week pilot program to test value-offerings at 1,900 U.S. locations. The company is testing different "mix and match bundles" to see which will drive sales, he said. McDonald's plans to launch the bundles most popular with customers nationwide in 2027, Kempczinski said. The news came after McDonald's earnings report, released Wednesday, showed comparable sales growth fell 0.2% at U.S. locations from July to September, after growing 2.4% during the same period last year. Overall foot traffic at the chain's U.S. stores was down 4.6% from a year ago, according to data from analytics platform Placer.ai.Kempczinski acknowledged that the company has not done enough to meet the expectations of low-income diners, who are looking for "great entry-level value.""We talked quite extensively about how [in] Q2 we didn't land that like we needed to," he told investors. "And so that's what we're in the midst of getting resolved right now and through testing."His comments come the day after the U.S. midterms, where affordability concerns took center stage. Many candidates campaigned on addressing cost-of-living issues and bringing down gasoline prices, which have risen 38% since the start of the war in Iran, according to AAA data.U.S. consumer spending has remained resilient even in the face of stubborn inflation, which remains stuck above the Federal Reserve's 2% target. However, economists note that lower-income consumers are feeling particularly strapped, as a larger share of their income goes toward expenses like gas.Low-income consumers "are disproportionately feeling the effect of higher food and gasoline prices," Ryan Sweet, chief global economist at Oxford Economics, said on Wednesday during an event in New York City.

Shares in Elon Musk's SpaceX have plunged as tech and artificial intelligence stocks more broadly plummeted a day after the Democrats swept to victory in the midterms.

Those losses dragged the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite stock index down, which had fallen by more than 5% at one point in early trading.

The market has been reacting to possible tougher scrutiny of data centre construction and the artificial intelligence (AI) industry following Democrat wins in key data centre states including Texas.

Following the election, some tech leaders have acknowledged they need to improve their communication around data centres and the benefits of AI.

SpaceX shares were down more than 7% in early trading on Thursday, while Tesla shares dropped more than 9%.

Musk had spent nearly $450m backing Republican campaigns, including at least $45m in support of Ken Paxton for the Texas senate seat, but Texas was turned blue in the Democratic tsunami on Tuesday night.

Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa campaigned heavily against data centres, pledging a moratorium on new construction in the sector.

Shares in chipmakers have been suffering, with AMD dropping nearly 17% over the past five days, while Micron shares have plunged more than 20%.

national.title: The election brought a wave of historic firsts. Here are some groundbreaking winners
national.summary: While some of these candidates have avoided focusing on the inherent historic value of their race, gender, religion or sexual orientation, some voters' rights advocates are celebrating how the electorate has expanded.
national.body:
Yes, the 2026 midterms will be remembered for the astonishing number of losses that Democrats handed to President Donald Trump. But in the background, something perhaps equally seismic unfolded: a wave of firsts that elevated into high office members of groups that had, until now, been kept largely at the margins.

WATCH: New Mexico's Deb Haaland on making history as first Native American woman elected governor

There were cheers and happy tears at election parties from New Mexico to Georgia late Tuesday once it became clear voters had elected the country's first Black female governor, the first Native American female governor, the first Native female senator and the first openly gay male U.S. senator. By early Wednesday, the first Muslim U.S. senator was also added to the list of barrier-breaking milestones. The astonishing blue wave also means the United States will likely have its first-ever Black speaker of the House.

Most of these firsts are Democrats, but the GOP has also broken some new ground.

While some of these candidates have avoided focusing on the inherent historic value of their race, gender, religion or sexual orientation, some voters' rights advocates are celebrating how the electorate has expanded.

"These firsts show how our country is changing," Alexis Anderson-Reed, president and CEO of State Voices, a network of advocates for civic engagement and equity in democracy, said via e-mail.

"For years, people of color and LGBTQ+ communities have organized, knocked on doors, talked to voters, held conversations, and done the hard work of saving our democracy," Anderson-Reed said. "These wins are because of them."

national.title: Discursive Verses: Is 'Spend Dat' the best financial indicator of America's grift economy?
national.summary: NPR Music culture critic and reporter Rodney Carmichael ruminates on the latest in rap culture. This week: How Yung Miami's summer bop became a sweeping indictment.
national.body:
After spending three hours counting the pores on Elizabeth Holmes' and Nathan Fielder's faces, I couldn't help but think how perfect Yung Miami's " Spend Dat " would've played over the closing credits. Whatever you feel about the veracity of the protagonist in the blockbuster doc You Can See Everything , there is no doubt about her innate ability to cop and blow money fast. She's probably about as familiar with Diddy's favorite City Girl as she is with Abbott & Costello. But a scammer of such ill repute deserves an apropos theme song. Hell, maybe we all do.

When people complain about hip-hop no longer being political, what they're really talking about is commercial rap's long-fizzled countercultural agenda. The politics of consumption and corruption however have never enjoyed a louder ringing endorsement. Like a billionaire hogging the bully pulpit. To that end, no song in 2026 comes closer to mimicking the feeling of being the violated and the violator. On its face, " Spend Dat " is a get-money flex dedicated to all the "scammers" and "booster b*****s." But behind that seductive veneer is the sadomasochistic loop of late-stage capitalism's long, punishing con. An inflation indicator like no other, it's easily our most American anthem of the year. And we're all transfixed, nodding along in unblinking commitment to the charade.

The video for " Spend Dat " feels like a throwback to the early 2000s, when making it rain in strip clubs was still obligatory signposting for selling the dream. It almost feels trite now that prediction markets allow us to place digital bets on democracy and buy-now, pay-later loans keep expanding on our freedom to fall deeper in debt. At least a good lap dance came with a tangible return on investment. Now we're all just being teased to death.

When India.Arie echoed the public denouncement of " Spend Dat " — which included a call for Black folk to boycott the Billboard -charting song of the summer — another film, I Love Boosters , had just hit streaming. Unlike the aforementioned documentary on the blonde-haired, blue-eyed, white-collar scammer Holmes, rapper-turned-director Boots Riley's fictional narrative centered on the supposed scourge of the hood. In it, Keke Palmer plays an illegit booster, selling high-end fenced clothing out of the abandoned fast-food chicken joint she's squatting in while harboring her own fashionable aspirations. It takes an international worker-led intervention — and a sci-fi bopgun full of Marxist intentions — for her to realize the minor disruption she and her shoplifting girlfriends are causing is but a necessary cog in the ever-churning, exploitative wheel of global capitalism.

Comedian and actor Russell Brand reflected in a car window as he left Southwark Crown Court in London on Monday. Alberto Pezzali/AP hide caption

London — Russell Brand was convicted Thursday of rape and sexual assault charges involving four women on allegations dating back more than 20 years.

Judge Joel Bennathan said the British actor-comedian faces a "significant" prison term when he is sentenced Monday. Brand had been free, but the judge rejected a bail request because of the possibility he might flee and he was taken into custody.

"I regret the hardship caused to the children, of course," the judge said. "But the hardship has been caused by serious criminal offending by their father."

Brand was a ruthless, calculating, manipulative "sexual predator," prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones said at trial.

Brand, 51, denied the charges and testified that he was obsessed with sex as a young man and once led a promiscuous life but had never forced anyone to do something against their will.

He was convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. He was acquitted of two rape counts and one count of attempted indecent assault.

Brand closed his eyes as the guilty verdict on the rape count was read but showed no emotion otherwise. When bail was denied, he gestured to his lawyers that he was OK and repeatedly said, "I'm good, I'm good, I'm good," before being taken away.

national.title: Americans wary of AI for medical care and insurance claims
national.summary: Most Americans have qualms about using AI in healthcare for tasks such as diagnosis and treatment, Pew Research poll finds.
national.body: How much artificial intelligence is too much when you visit your doctor? Although patients are generally open to healthcare professionals using AI to handle administrative and some medical tasks, they want humans wielding the stethoscope, a recent survey suggests.A solid majority of Americans are comfortable with AI translating patient notes or scheduling appointments, either on its own or with some human oversight, according to the Pew Research Center, which polled more than 3,400 U.S. adults in June. More than half the respondents were also open to using AI to analyze medical scans and lab test results, provided a healthcare professional supervised the process.But people draw the line when it comes to AI driving diagnoses or making insurance decisions, Pew found. Almost half of those surveyed said they don't want an AI model deciding whether to accept or reject an insurance claim, while 41% said they don't want AI making a diagnosis on its own.Galen Stocking, associate director of science and society research at Pew Research Center, said people see value in applying AI to healthcare. Still, patients want to know when and how healthcare providers and administrative staff are using the technology."Overall, people say it's extremely important that their healthcare provider tell them if they are using AI," he told CBS News. "There is a lack of clarity on the side of the public," he added, noting Pew's finding that 46% of the survey respondents said they don't know if AI has ever been used in the course of them receiving care.Indeed, 60% of respondents said they are uncomfortable with doctors using AI for tasks such as diagnosis and treatment; only 30% are OK with that, while 10% are unsure. "People are concerned about patient-doctor relationships and the security of their own health information," Stocking said. More broadly, Americans are split over whether AI will improve the quality of medical care. Some 37% of respondents said AI will improve health outcomes, while a nearly equal share think the technology could reduce the quality of care.

It's been an extraordinary night for the Democrats in the US midterms.

They have taken control of the Senate and the House of Representatives too.

Texas , Iowa , Ohio and Maine also turned blue and the Democrats held Michigan . There are two seats remaining, Alaska and Mississippi , both are on a knife edge.

The shift from Republican to Democrat happened across the country. Some of the biggest swings since the presidential election in 2024 were in Texas where the Democrats took the Senate seat and the governor. Several counties on the state's southern border swung by more that 50 percentage points.

More victims are likely to come forward following his conviction, the detective who led the police investigation has said.

national.body:
Protests are taking place across France after five unions launched a national day of strike action, joining high school students and demonstrators criticising the rising cost of living.

More than 250,000 people had taken to the streets in almost 70 towns and cities by 13:00 (12:00 GMT) on Thursday, and that was "just the start", said Sophie Binet of the CGT union.

The unions have vowed to take the wave of protests that began in September over poor conditions and resources at lycées (high schools) "to the next level".

They have since spread to include workers and the so-called "yellow-vest" movement against high prices.

Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said 70,000 police were being deployed, vowing "an extremely firm response" to any potential outbreaks of violence.

Some unrest has been reported in the cities of Lyon and Rennes.

A car was set alight near the Gallieni bridge over the Rhône river in central Lyon, as hundreds of people belonging to the radical left-wing "black bloc" clashed with police.

Meanwhile, there were clashes in the north-western city of Rennes, where the local prefect said a "hostile group of masked individuals" had gathered in front of the main union march.

LONDON (AP) — Russell Brand was convicted Thursday of rape and sexual assault charges on allegations dating back more than 20 years.

Judge Joel Bennathan said Brand faces a "significant" prison term when he is sentenced Monday. He had been free on bail but was taken into custody.

A prosecutor said the British actor-comedian was a ruthless, calculating, manipulative "sexual predator."

Brand, 51, denied the charges and testified that he was obsessed with sex as a young man and once led a promiscuous life but had never forced anyone to do something against their will.

national.title: First-time homebuyers remain scarce, but a record share of them pay all cash
national.summary: A new report finds generational wealth is widening the divide between homebuyers and those priced out. The median age of first-time buyers also remains at a record high.
national.body:
The share of first-time homebuyers remains at a near-record low of 22% as a housing shortage and high prices sideline many, according to a new report by the National Association of Realtors. But those who are managing to buy are older and wealthier than in the past, and 1 in 10 paid all cash, a record high since such data was collected starting in 2003.

"Inheritances are really driving this," said Jessica Lautz, deputy chief economist at the NAR.

First-time buyers who paid all-cash were more likely than those who financed a house to use an inheritance (28%) or proceeds from the sale of an inherited property (21%). They were also older.

NAR finds the median age of all first-time buyers remains at 40, a record high. For first-time buyers who financed a purchase it was 38, while for those who paid all-cash it was 54. "They waited a significant period of time for that generational transfer of wealth to come through," Lautz said.

Affordability How long does it take to save up for a starter home? Twice as long as it did in 2019 For first-time buyers overall, personal savings was the biggest source of funding for a down payment. But in another shift, more people used assets – like a 401(k), stocks, or cryptocurrency – than financial help from family or friends. Older buyers have had more time to save up, Lautz said, but she thinks there's another factor: "I think it's uncomfortable to ask mom and dad for a gift or loan when you're hitting 40 versus your young 30s."

The share of first time buyers using an inheritance is likely to grow in coming years as boomers reach their 80's and beyond. As the report noted, "there is a growing divide among those who are saving independently and priced out of homeownership, versus those who are waiting on the sidelines but then given a generational transfer of wealth."

Your Money Here's the latest sticker shock: Borrowing for a mortgage — or a car Real estate agents around the country are seeing the change.

"I would say in the first 15 years of my career, I saw virtually zero first-time home buyers paying all cash," said Jason Miller, a broker with Trust Real Estate Company in St. Cloud, Minn.

national.title: Six dead and others injured in fire at New York City building
national.summary: The cause of the blaze is not yet clear, after 230 fire and emergency medical personnel went to the scene.
national.body:
Six people have died after a large fire broke out in a residential building in Brooklyn, New York City, officials say.

Several others were hurt in the blaze, which occurred early on Thursday morning, the New York City Fire Department (FDNY) said in a statement.

More than 230 fire and emergency medical personnel were sent to the scene near Sunset Park after the fire was first reported at around 01:40 local time (06:40 GMT).

Mayor Zohran Mamdani said he was "heartbroken" by the deaths, and has asked New Yorkers to "take a moment to pray for the full recovery of those who were injured".

A crew specialising in hazardous materials was sent to the scene because of the presence of a lithium-ion battery, although it was not clear whether this was linked to the blaze.

The emergency responders reportedly discovered on their arrival that the building's first and second floors had been engulfed by flames.

Four individuals were pronounced dead at the scene, according to the FDNY.

A male and female were also taken to the hospital, where they were pronounced dead, the New York City Police Department (NYPD) said.

national.title: A bitter end for Ronaldo - the icon who transformed Portugal
national.summary: As Cristiano Ronaldo retires from international football, Guillem Balague looks at why and what is next for the Portugal legend.
national.body:
BBC Sport Columnist Published 3 hours ago Cristiano Ronaldo's old rival Leo Messi left Argentina less than a month ago with a nation applauding him.

The Portugal legend has gone another way, and it was always going to be the case.

The 41-year-old announced his international retirement after 23 years but also after a fallout with coach Jorge Jesus which was resolved with a sanction of 30 days, that had already been served, and a fine of 255 euros.

It was the punishment imposed on the Portuguese striker for leaving the team's training camp without permission. Jesus kept him on the bench for one match and said he did not plan to start him in the next, so Ronaldo went home.

His last appearance came on 24 September against Wales. He ends his international career with 146 goals in 234 games.

A message went around Portugal with a big thank you for everything, calling Ronaldo a global ambassador and an inspiration to millions. Even so, the way it ended leaves a bit of a bitter taste.

Was he going to be named in the next squad? Possibly, as Jesus said the door was open and the decision was Ronaldo's. What is clear is that he was no longer an automatic starter, and Cristiano has never handled that well.

So is this another hissy fit? Partly, yes. He reacted the way he always has when a coach questions his place. But the label hides how much he adapted over the years.

Democrat Scott Colom and Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith are locked in a tight race for a US Senate seat in Mississippi, a state that has not elected a Democratic candidate to the upper chamber in more than 40 years.

With 96% of votes counted as of Thursday morning, Colom was leading by just over 1,000 votes.

Hyde-Smith, the first woman to represent Mississippi in the US Congress, was elected in 2018 and has been endorsed by Donald Trump. The president won the state by more than 22 points in 2024.

If Colom wins the race, he would be the first black US senator elected in Mississippi since 1875.

"We remain confident that when every legally cast vote is fully and accurately counted, Mississippians will have reelected Cindy Hyde-Smith," the incumbent's campaign said in a statement.

national.title: Joshua Wong, face of Hong Kong's pro-democracy protests, jailed for 10 years
national.summary: Wong, 30, is among hundreds of Hongkongers detained under the controversial national security law.
national.body:
Joshua Wong, once the face of Hong Kong's democracy movement, has been sentenced to 10 years in jail for colluding with foreign forces under the city's sweeping national security law.

Wong is among hundreds of campaigners and ordinary Hongkongers arrested under the law, which was imposed in 2020 following explosive pro-democracy protests against Beijing's growing control.

Critics say the far-reaching law has silenced dissent, but authorities argue that it is needed to maintain stability and deny it has weakened the city's cherished autonomy.

Having already spent the last six years in jail, Wong, who was due to be freed in January, will now spend another decade behind bars.

On Thursday, he arrived in court wearing a dark blue long-sleeved shirt, khaki trousers and black-rimmed glasses. He looked slimmer compared to his previous public appearances.

national.title: Melania Trump hosting Russian and Ukrainian delegations at the White House
national.summary: On Wednesday, Ukraine gave Melania Trump an award for her "significant personal contribution to humanitarian support".
national.body:
US First Lady Melania Trump is hosting Russian and Ukrainian delegations at the White House on Thursday, a day after being given Ukraine's highest award for women by President Volodymyr Zelensky.

The Order of Princess Olha, 1st Class, was awarded to Melania Trump for her "significant personal contribution to humanitarian support for Ukraine", according to the presidential decree.

It comes after the end of ceasefire in Ukraine's southern region of Kherson, which allowed for the evacuation of several hundred people from the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky .

The delegations from Kyiv and Moscow are made up of ombudsmen who were involved in the evacuation mission as well as senior officials.

The White House said that Melania Trump had "independently initiated engagement between the two warring nations and successfully secured a ceasefire".

"This achievement marks an unprecedented diplomatic initiative by an American First Lady", it added.

Both the Russian and Ukrainian sides repeatedly thanked Melania Trump for brokering the ceasefire, though neither elaborated on the nature or extent of her involvement.

The delegations travelling to the White House on Thursday will include Ukraine's human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets and his Russian counterpart Yana Lantratova, as well as Ukrainian MP Davyd Arakhamia and Russian senior official Kirill Dmitriev.

local.title: Blue wave misses area; Borrello, Molitor re-elected
local.summary: The blue wave that flipped offices from red to blue on Election Day is costing Republicans in the New York state Legislature as well. Statewide, it appears Democrats have reimagined their supermajorities in both the state Senate and state Assembly after flipping at least a dozen seats, including fiv
local.body:
The blue wave that flipped offices from red to blue on Election Day is costing Republicans in the New York state Legislature as well.

Statewide, it appears Democrats have reimagined their supermajorities in both the state Senate and state Assembly after flipping at least a dozen seats, including five on Long Island. Long Island's 31-member legislative delegation will remain largely Republican, but Democrats won enough seats there to extend their legislative majorities. The supermajority means Democrats can override a veto by Gov. Kathy Hochul, though the threatened override hasn't come into play often in the past.

“This achievement reflects the strength of our diverse coalition, representing communities from our largest cities to our smallest towns, and our shared commitment to moving New York forward," Senate Majority Leader Andrea Stewart-Cousins, D-Yonkers, said in a statement shortly before midnight on Tuesday.

Locally, the blue wave didn't affect state Sen. George Borrello or Assemblyman Andrew Molitor. The Republicans retained their seats, with Molitor winning re-election. With all districts reporting, Molitor received 26,485 votes while challenger Thomas A. Carle received 15,490 votes. Borrello won Chautauqua County’s vote for the 57th Senate District, 28,037-14,502 over challenger Victoria Guite-Williams. With all but one election district reporting across the 57th Senate District Borrello received 78,049 votes (68.04%) to Guite-Williams’ 33,922 votes (29.57%).

"I am humbled and grateful to the people of the 57th District for once again electing me to be their voice in Albany," Borrello said in a statement. "Over the past six years, I’ve worked hard to build a record that reflects the priorities of the people I represent. That means standing up for taxpayers, fighting for our farmers and small businesses, challenging costly energy mandates and working to keep our communities safe. I’ve never been afraid to speak out or take on a difficult fight when the well-being of the people I represent is at stake. The concerns I’ve heard from residents about affordability, energy policy, public safety and other key issues will continue to drive my work in Albany. We’ve made progress on some important issues, but there’s much more to do. I’ll keep fighting for policies that will reverse the decline we've experienced under one-party rule and the outmigration that has resulted. New York has so many assets and potential. With the right policies, we can be the Empire State again."

local.body:
PORTLAND -- As Portland Supervisor Rich Lewis said at a recent Brocton Village Board meeting, "Code Enforcement is going through some changes."

Moving forward, the town of Portland and the village of Brocton will rely on Roger Britz Jr. as a part-time Code Enforcement Officer. Britz, of Fredonia, will work up to 20 hours per week over the course of the year. His hours will fluctuate depending on need.

There will also be a full-time Code Clerk dedicated to the clerical duties of the Code Enforcement Office. That position is open and will be filled in the near future. In the meantime, the town of Portland is relying on part-time clerical support.

"We are looking to have someone hired as soon as possible for that," Lewis said.

Britz fills a void left by Joshua Dobbs, who is no longer employed by the town of Portland. Dobbs was initially hired in March as a town-wide provisional Inspection Officer to serve both the town of Portland and the village of Brocton. Dobbs was recently out on medical leave, with former Code Enforcement Officer Wendy Spinuzza helping the two municipalities with code-related matters in the interim on an hourly basis.

The changes were made "after careful assessment and talk with Mayor (Craig) Miller", Lewis said. The shift will make the Code Enforcement Office more accessible for residents, Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. each week. Britz was appointed to the role on Oct. 14, and since then, Lewis said "he has made major strides." Britz has worked closely with Spinuzza as he gets up to speed in the new role.

"I think it's going to work out much better than what we've had in recent times," Lewis said.

One of the most notable properties in the village of Brocton that does not comply with the village code is 98 Old Mill Road, where a home was destroyed in a fatal fire on Christmas morning of 2024. The property has yet to be cleaned up.

local.body:
Rep. Nick Langworthy will remain the 23rd Congressional representative in Congress, though he will be taking on a different role in the House minority when the new Congress is seated in January.

Langworthy defeated Aaron Gies of Olean, 59.4% to 39.15%, with Langworthy receiving 181,807 of the 305,882 ballots cast. Langworthy won each county in the district, 68.19% to 29.85% in Allegany County, 64.8% to 33.75% in Cattaraugus County, 58.35% to 40.34% in Chemung County, 56.72% to 41.87% in Erie County, 58.82% to 39.52% in Niagara County, 65.15% to 33.65% in Schuyler County, 63.76% to 35.03% in Steuben County and 58.23% to 40.37% in Tioga County. The most ballots in the race were cast in Erie County (130,320) and Chautauqua County (43,293).

"Last night's election results are a win for common sense and the truth. The people of Western New York and the Southern Tier sent a loud and clear message that they know I fight for them in Washington. The results are a powerful affirmation of my record of putting more money in taxpayers' pockets, making our communities safer, strengthening rural healthcare, and protecting their access to affordable, reliable energy," Langworthy said early Wednesday morning. "This is where I was born and raised, and where I am raising my own family. The people of this district are why I fight–for a better future for them, their children, and their grandchildren. While we are forgotten by Albany, I will always make sure our region has a seat at the table in Washington."

Results in the 23rd District race indicate Republicans in Chautauqua County may not have turned out in as great a number as they did in 2024. Gies received 17,129 votes in Chautauqua County, slightly fewer votes than the 17,491 votes Tom Carle received when challenging Langworthy two years ago. That’s a decrease of roughly 2.1% from 2024 to 2026. Langworthy received 25,564 votes in Chautauqua County and 36,798 in 2024, a 30.5% decrease from two years ago.

The House of Representatives that Langworthy has been re-elected to will have a much different look.

Democrats have won control of Congress in Tuesday's 2026 midterm elections. Democrats flipped at least seven Senate seats in red states and battlegrounds alike: Kansas, which hasn't elected a Democratic senator in nearly a century, Iowa, Texas, Ohio, Maine, North Carolina and South Carolina. They held on to battleground seats in Georgia and Michigan. In the House, Democrats flipped more than two dozen districts, some that voted for Trump by double digits in 2024.

local.title: The OBSERVER’s View: Hochul needs to quit delaying on Kyra’s Law
local.summary: We’ve reached the time of year when Gov. Kathy Hochul begins signing legislation passed by the state Legislature before the end of its session in June. It’s ludicrous to us that this process takes half a year in some cases, particularly when it comes to legislation that was approved with overwhelmin
local.body:
We’ve reached the time of year when Gov. Kathy Hochul begins signing legislation passed by the state Legislature before the end of its session in June.

It’s ludicrous to us that this process takes half a year in some cases, particularly when it comes to legislation that was approved with overwhelming legislative support like Kyra’s Law (A.6194-C/S.5998). Kyra's Law is named in memory of 2-year-old Kyra Franchettie, who was shot and killed by her father during a court-ordered unsupervised visit in 2016, and was passed with bipartisan support in the state Legislature this year. It remains unsigned four months after the end of the legislative session and was raised by several local women who spoke with The Post-Journal on their experiences dealing with the aftermath of domestic violence. Kyra’s Law doesn’t just help women, though. There are cases in which men who have been awarded custody of their children deal with many of the same issues that the sponsors of Kyra’s Law are trying to deal with.

Kyra’s Law isn’t a cure-all for domestic violence, but two of the women who spoke with The Post-Journal and OBSERVER said it would likely help make their situations better. Kyra’s Law would require courts to conduct a review in custody and visitation proceedings involving allegations of domestic violence, child abuse or substantial risks of harm to a child warranting the court’s immediate attention. It would expand the evidence a court considers to include risk factors, such as threats to harm or kill, stalking, violence during pregnancy, unlawful dissemination of intimate images, coercive control and a recent pattern of substance abuse, It would also permit review of certain uncertified records in proceedings for temporary visitation and custody; allow waiver of notice in emergency ex parte applications; and make substantial risk findings a significant factor in custody and visitation determinations. Kyra's Law would also expand custody and visitation procedures in state Supreme Court by requiring courts to advise parties of counsel rights; require courts to explain on the record the basis for custody and visitation determinations; prohibit adverse inferences against protective parents or assumptions regarding a child’s reluctance to interact with a parent; and require recurring judicial training on child safety and domestic violence’ issues.

"I can honestly say after being through all of this, the worst agony is watching your child suffer and nobody can help," said one of the women. "I literally felt like I could die. That is the worst agony to ever go through; the emotional abuse and fear is worse than the physical. It affects your whole life. They're not connecting how detrimental this is to children and mothers, what these criminals are doing."

local.body:
For me, communications in 2026 boil down to telephone, texting, or email. I don't do smoke signals anymore.

Alas, my arthritic hands have consigned hand-written notes to the back burner. When I hand write, maybe the first line or two have some resemblance to my once clear penmanship. Then the fingers cramp, the wrist stops pushing, and the script becomes a scrawl rapidly descending towards chicken scratch. Sort of like a doctor's prescription.

So, with my handwriting on the fritz, the computer has become my favorite. I still like to send a handwritten personal greeting. But if it extends past two handwritten lines, the remainder is a printout, folded and inserted with the card or note. I write the envelope at a different time so it's legible enough for the post office's machine readers.

My computer is my lifeline. Because of this column and a bunch of other writerly commitments, I'm on my laptop first thing in the morning and last thing at night. My knotty, knobby fingers much prefer the keyboard to texting. The text letters and numbers on my phone are too tiny for my stiff joints - I only text as a last resort. Then just last week, I learned to hate my phones. Plural.

Yes, we still have a land line. We are probably one of the three or four families left in Warren who are still paying two phone bills. No, it's not because we have money to burn. It's because without the land line, we wouldn't have a way to find our cell phones!

The insurance people who sell Medicare programs have been constantly calling since the middle of October. They have until the first week in December to convince me - and oodles of other seniors – that we should change our insurance to their plan. I don't know how many insurers are out there trying to change my mind, but if I judge it by the telephone traffic, it's hundreds. They start promptly at 9:00 a.m. every weekday. At first, I was simply frustrated by the frequency. I listened to a few to get the gist of things. When I say "Hello," there is the telltale pause. Then a voice says hello... with an uplifted question mark at the end of the word. So of course, that's when I repeat our hello, which kicks on the recorded sales statement.

"Hello, this is Naomi. We have been trying to reach you for a week ...." Or, "This is Jennifer responding to your call for more insurance information...." No, I did not inquire about your insurance. And yes, if you've been trying for a week, it's because I don't want to talk to you. Leave me alone. PU-LEEZ. The number of these calls is ridiculously out of hand. It took me until this week to find the BLOCK button on the bottom of my landline receiver.

Upon investigation, I found she is a learned woman with a bachelor's degree from Cornell and a Masters of International Affairs from Columbia University. In addition, she is fluent in both Arabic and Swahili. Following 9/11 she was recruited by the Central Intelligence Agency as a Middle East Analyst and served three tours in Iraq over a period of five years.

Following that she served on the National Security Council during the George W. Bush Administration and was asked to stay on during the President Barack Obama Administration. She later served in senior leadership roles at the Department of Defense, eventually serving as the Acting Assistant Secretary of Defense for International Affairs. Mike Rogers.

During her political career, Slotkin has been controversial but after remarks made at a political forum at the University of Chicago on Oct. 13, she rose to new heights of controversial speech. She advocated pursuing what she called "signature cases" involving President Trump and those around him. She said, "I want to look at these signature cases not focusing on the president but on the people who enabled him. local.summary: First responders who went above and beyond to save lives were recognized Wednesday night during Mercy Hospital’s annual EMS Awards Dinner.
local.body: First responders who went above and beyond to save lives were recognized Wednesday night during Mercy Hospital’s annual EMS Awards Dinner.The event honored emergency medical crews whose quick actions made a difference during life-threatening emergencies, including the rescue of a 34-year-old man found face down in a backyard.For Skip Yuhnke, a paramedic with the Elma Fire Department, the call was a reminder of why he has dedicated nearly five decades to emergency medical services.“I got a monitor on him and I gave him one shock, but it took a lot more than that to get him to come around and get pulses and to start breathing again,” Yuhnke said.Despite his years of experience, Yuhnke said successfully bringing someone back after cardiac arrest is rare, making calls like this especially meaningful.“When you get somebody that comes back and you can actually save them, or you make their life better, or you help them so they do have a better outcome in their life, that's what it's all about to me,” he said.Next year, Yuhnke will mark 50 years as an EMT.Kenneth Peterson, deputy fire commissioner for EMS with Buffalo Fire, said the awards dinner recognizes the dedication of first responders who put their communities first.“They are individuals that come from all walks of life that choose to both volunteer, compensated, to wake up in the middle of the night at a moment's notice and respond to calls for service, typically medical in nature,” Peterson said.Peterson said the dinner is also an opportunity to recognize those who often put their own busy lives aside to help others.Elizabeth Forkel with Erie County MERS said first responders do not always receive the recognition they deserve, despite the long hours and sacrifices they make.“A lot of first responders go unrecognized for their work. local.title: Buffalo Guinea Pig Mafia Rescue over capacity after taking in more than 20 guinea pigs in three weeks
local.summary: The Williamsville-based rescue is seeking medical foster homes and donations to help care for more than 100 guinea pigs, including 13 recently rescued from Syracuse.
local.body: A Western New York animal rescue is asking for the community's help after taking in more than 20 guinea pigs in just three weeks, leaving the organization over capacity.The Buffalo Guinea Pig Mafia Rescue, based in Williamsville, currently cares for approximately 112 guinea pigs, according to Executive Director Jessica Meacham.Among the recent arrivals are 13 guinea pigs from Syracuse that came to the rescue severely malnourished and with fight wounds. Several required shaving and antiseptic medication, and all have needed additional medical care.Meacham said three of the females may also be pregnant.The influx has created additional challenges for the small organization, which typically houses 15 to 20 guinea pigs at its rescue center. Cages are now being placed on floors and tables, with some double-stacked to accommodate the growing population."It's been really tough for us because we're a small organization," Meacham said. "Taking in 20 at any one given time, especially 20 that have severe medical needs, is really hard."WATCH: Buffalo Guinea Pig Mafia Rescue over capacity after taking in more than 20 guinea pigs in three weeksHow the community can helpThe rescue's biggest immediate need is medical foster homes. Meacham said finding temporary homes for five or six guinea pigs would help ease overcrowding and allow the organization to return to its typical setup.The rescue provides foster families with cages, hay, pellets and vitamin C. Foster families are responsible for providing fresh vegetables and helping with the animals' daily care.The organization is also accepting donations of:HayUnscented paper beddingUnscented laundry detergentAll donated supplies must be new and unopened.The rescue typically goes through two to three bags of hay each day, making supply donations especially important.Those interested in fostering, donating or learning more can contact the Buffalo Guinea Pig Mafia Rescue through its Facebook page. The organization's Amazon wish list is can be found here. Meacham said the need for help continues to grow, but community support can make a difference in giving these guinea pigs the care and attention they need.

local.title: Buffalo voters approve all 11 proposed changes to city charter
local.summary: Buffalo voters approved all 11 proposed changes to the city charter on Election Day, giving the green light to a series of changes involving how city government operates.
local.body: Buffalo voters approved all 11 proposed changes to the city charter on Election Day, giving the green light to a series of changes involving how city government operates.The city charter essentially serves as the rule book for Buffalo city government. All 11 ballot measures passed Tuesday, with even the closest proposal approved by 33 percentage points.“I think it was great. I think people paid attention to it,” said Laurence Rubin, chair of the City of Buffalo Charter Revision Commission.The commission worked with members of the community to fine-tune the proposals before they were put before voters.The newly approved measures cover a range of issues, including clarifying mayoral succession, reviewing inactive city boards and creating new community-driven commissions.One of those is a new Civilian Police Advisory Commission, which is intended to provide more opportunities for the public to engage on issues involving community policing."More interaction, more communication, more opportunity for the public to be heard about their concerns," Rubin said. "And I think that at least our current administration seems to be interested in hearing that."WATCH: Buffalo voters approve all 11 proposed changes to city charterAnother approved measure amends the city charter to establish a Commission on Human Rights, focused on the protection and promotion of human rights for Buffalo residents."They can look at issues about how local government, city government, is dealing with issues of human rights, or impacting on human rights in the City of Buffalo," Rubin said. "But it actually has a broader mandate that it can go beyond that and look community-wide at issues about human rights."Rubin said many of the charter changes take effect immediately, while the process of creating the newly approved commissions is expected to take a couple of months.With voters approving all 11 measures, Buffalo will now begin implementing the charter changes. While many provisions can take effect immediately, Rubin said establishing the new commissions will require additional time.

entertainment.title: Nicki Minaj Is Battling Her Own Lawyers in Both L.A. and NYC: ‘A Breakdown in Communication’
entertainment.summary: The star’s attorneys are desperately trying to fire her in the Big Apple while her former Hollywood lawyers are suing her for nearly $300,000 in unpaid legal fees.
entertainment.body:
Nicki Minaj is no stranger to litigation. But she’s increasingly a stranger to her own lawyers.

In a New York case filed against her earlier this year by a concert production company, Minaj’s legal team at Kurzman Eisenberg Corbin & Lever is currently trying to withdraw because their relationship with the rapper has “irretrievably broken down.” But they say she’s refused to let them.

“KECL has done everything within its power,” the firm writes in a Tuesday (Nov. 4) court filing, asking the judge to allow it to immediately pull out from the case.

The New York case was filed last year by 24/7 Productions, which claims Minaj has refused to reimburse $275,000 spent on her iHeartRadio’s 2023 Jingle Ball concerts and later that year for shows tied to her album Pink Friday 2 . The company said it made “many attempts” over two years to get the money but that the star’s team had “never given a reason” for failing to pay.

Minaj’s lawyers have denied the claims in court , calling the case “an ill-advised attempt to sue a famous deep-pocket.” But late last month, the attorneys at Kurzman Eisenberg who made those arguments said they could no longer represent the star in the case due to “irreconcilable differences” that had arisen between them.

“Counsel and the Defendants have been unable to align on litigation strategy, and the attorney-client relationship has irretrievably broken down such that continued representation is no longer feasible or appropriate,” Bruce W. Bieber wrote in the Oct. 23 court filing. “There has also been a breakdown in communication.”

Then on Tuesday, Bieber asked the judge to relieve the firm immediately, saying they had been unable to even get Minaj to acknowledge their request to exit the case.

“The process server was advised that the concierge at Minaj’s residence was advised that somebody would come downstairs [for purposes of accepting the papers], but nobody came down,” Bieber wrote. “Finally … on November 2, 2026, the process server was advised that Minaj was not available and provided no further information.”

Previous recipients of the King of Comedy award are Adam Sandler in 2023 and Jack Black last year.

I’m grateful to Nickelodeon and CBS for this honor. And if I get slimed, just know I’ll be sending them my dry-cleaning bill.”

Alex Warren is set to host the show, which will be the first Kids Choice Awards show in 17 months.

Tyla hosted the last show, which aired in June 2025. Warren, who topped the Billboard Hot 100 for 10 weeks in 2025 with “Ordinary,” is the first male pop star to host the show since Nick Jonas in 2015.

Swift leads all individual nominees with six nods, followed by Ariana Grande and Sabrina Carpenter with five nods each. Kelce is nominated for favorite male sports star and favorite podcast for New Heights With Jason & Travis Kelce , which he hosts with his older brother Jason Kelce .

Grande, who has won twice for favorite song for “Bang Bang” (a collab with Jessie J and Nicki Minaj) and “Thank U, Next,” is nominated again in that category for “hate that i made you love me.” The other nominees in the category include one-time winners Justin Bieber, Carpenter, BTS and Swift, as well as Olivia Rodrigo, Bruno Mars and Benson Boone, who are looking for their first wins in the category.

entertainment.summary: "It brings back, really, a special time in my career," he tells Billboard Chart History of one of the videos.
entertainment.body:
Luke Bryan and Billboard are taking a walk down memory lane, as part of the Billboard Chart History series. Since the start of his career, Bryan has had 26 songs scale the pinnacle of Billboard ‘s Country Airplay chart. In his video with Billboard , Bryan discusses many of his biggest country chart hits, starting with his first Country Airplay No. 1, 2010’s “Rain Is a Good Thing.” Related Ozzfest Announces 2027 Return With Three-Date U.K./North American Run Rush Bringing Reunion Tour to Sphere With 'Elevate From the Norm' Residency Tate McRae, Olivia Rodrigo & Harry Styles: Which Pop Stars Won October 2026? (Greatest Pop Stars Podcast) Explore Luke Bryan See latest videos, charts and news

Bryan recalls how the music video conveyed where the Georgia native was in his career at that moment.

“I was right outside of my college town — I think it was our first Farm Tour show ever,” Bryan reflects. “The beauty of that video, is just really, really me in a nutshell. We didn’t have a super big video budget, we knew we had a great little show to video … it brings back, really, a special time in my career where I’m praying every day that I can build my career, and the best way to build your career is to have your first No. 1 song on Billboard , and obviously ‘Rain Is a Good Thing’ was that. I wrote it with one of my best friends in the world, [songwriter] Dallas Davidson. We were still relatively young writers, and we took a phrase [“Rain makes corn, corn makes whiskey”] we grew up hearing in South Georgia … the fact that we were able to take something we heard as young men, and go on to become my first Billboard No. 1, was really incredible.”

While the lighthearted “Rain Is a Good Thing” brought an initial career milestone, Bryan also talks about how the emotional 2014 hit “Drink a Beer” helped give his career new dimension.

“I think at the time I was known as the uptempo, really energetic, high-energy party guy, and so when I put ‘Drink a Beer’ out, it just really showed another depth of my artistry. I could have a very impactful song, with a deep subject matter, and the coolest aspect about it is Jim Beavers and Chris Stapleton wrote it, and at the time, the Nashville songwriting community, we were praying that the world would learn about Chris Stapleton the artist, not just the songwriter. And so, when I had the opportunity to perform ‘Drink a Beer’ at the CMAs [in 2013], I called Chris. That was like, maybe the year or so before [Chris] and Justin Timberlake had their [CMA Awards] moment [in 2015]. The bottom line was I was just really happy to share that moment with Chris. The lyrics of that song, the emotion of that song, spoke to a country audience as good as you could speak.”

entertainment.title: Nicki Minaj Reacts After Democrats Dominate in the 2026 Midterms: ‘Trump Is STILL Your PRESIDENT’
entertainment.summary: The rapper had urged followers to vote red, but Republicans lost control of Congress by a landslide.
entertainment.body:
Nicki Minaj has spoken out after the conclusion of the 2026 midterms, which saw Democrats overwhelmingly win in congressional and state elections across the country on Tuesday (Nov. 3).

The following day, the rapper — who has spent the past year campaigning for Donald Trump and his MAGA party — shared a speechless video on X of herself looking blankly into the camera while wearing pale blue contacts in her eyes and a black blazer. “Couple things,” she wrote, introducing a list of personal reminders led by: “1. Trump is STILL your PRESIDENT.”

“The QUEEN is STILL your OBSESSION,” she continued. “Jesus is STILL LORD … The BARBZ are STILL PRETTY!!! … Stay tuned & STAY MAD. … Maybe now our people will WAKE UP.”

Minaj also praised JD Vance’s “great insight” after the vice president shared a lengthy post about the Republican losses, claiming that the “real reason” voters didn’t back them was the United States’ war with Iran. The hip-hop star also congratulated conservative Florida politicians Anna Paulina Luna and Byron Donalds, who won their respective races for House of Representatives and governor.

Fans and critics alike had been waiting for what Minaj would say after Democrats resumed control of both the House and the Senate in a landslide victory Tuesday night, flipping dozens of congressional seats. Leading up to the election, she’d joined Trump on the campaign trail rallying support for Republican candidates, and on voting day, she posted an AI-generated image of Chucky wearing a “Vote Red” badge, which Child’s Play filmmaker Don Mancini roasted soon afterward. “Chucky says ‘A BLUE WAVE’ is coming, as BLUE as my f — kin’ eyes!” he wrote on X.

Though Minaj — who was born in Trinidad and Tobago — is not a U.S. citizen, she has become enmeshed in the Republican Party since late 2025, when she first started appearing at political events. She first met the twice-impeached POTUS in January at his Trump Accounts summit in Washington, D.C., calling herself his “No. 1 fan.”

“She’s been with me a long time,” the president said of Minaj during an Oval Office meeting in October, after which she told Barbz on X: “Not going anywhere.”

entertainment.title: Six Other Musicians Who’ve Had an Audience With Pope Leo
entertainment.summary: After Bob Dylan's hooded huddle with Pope Leo on Wednesday (Nov. 4) we look at other musical visits to the Vatican to commune with the American-born pontiff.
entertainment.body:
It was the bizarre photo that somehow managed to cut through all the dissection and celebration surrounding the Blue-nami Democratic wave wins in the midterm elections on Wednesday (Nov. 4). Bob Dylan, dressed in his by-now-familiar dark hoodie, hood up, meeting with the first American-born pontiff , Pope Leo XIV, at the Vatican.

Minnesota native Dylan — who performed for and met Pope John Paul II in 1997 — had a private audience with Chicago-bred Pope Leo during which he wore his hoodie, along with a black jacket, black zip-up, loosely tied polka dot black tie and black pants. According to the Vatican, the pope gave the Nobel Prize-winning folk icon a rosary and Dylan in turn gave the leader of the Catholic Church a copy of his Chronicles: Volume One memoir.

Though the sight of the two men launched hundreds of memes and quips about their big mismatched crime-solving duo energy, it was not the first time the American Pope has met with a popular musician or hosted them at the Vatican for a special event. In fact, the 71-year-old religious leader whose papacy began on May 8, 2025 has met with a number and hosted special events with a number of rock, pop, opera and Latin artists since ascending to the papacy last year.

From meeting with punk legend Patti Smith, Bad Bunny and Italian singer Laura Pausini, to attending concerts by crooner Michael Bublé and Italian conductor Riccardo Muti, Pope Leo has enjoyed audiences with a number of bold-faced names, in addition to overseeing (but not attending) last September’s Grace for the World show in St. Peter’s Square that featured Bocelli, Karol G, Pharrell Williams, John Legend and Jennifer Hudson.

Check out a list of six of Pope Leo’s top musical encounter moments below.

Italian pop singer Pausini received Billboard Italy’s prestigious Global Icon award on Nov. 12, 2025 during a historic Vatican ceremony with Pope Leo. “I’m very excited and honored to have received the Global Icon award in the presence of the Pope,” Pausini told Billboard Italy. “It was a moment and an encounter that I will remember forever. I wanted to offer Him what represents my very soul, my voice and my music.” In addition, Pausini presented the pope with a unique, unreleased song, her rendition of “Brother Sun, Sister Moon,” which was inspired by Saint Francis of Assisi’s “Canticle of the Creatures.”

Considered one of the music industry’s most prestigious honors, the Songwriters Hall of Fame recognizes both performing writers, and the lesser-recognized non-performing pens behind pop’s biggest hits. Also on the list this year is Stargate, the producer duo whose credits include Katy Perry’s “Firework” and Rihanna’s “Diamonds,” as well as Dan Wilson, who co-wrote Adele’s “Someone Like You” and Semisonic’s “Closing Time.”

The songwriting trio of Stock Aitken Waterman, who wrote Rick Astley’s “Never Gonna Give You Up,”made the ballot this year, as did the trio of Bob Feldman, Jerry Goldstein and Richard Gottehrer, who wrote “I Want Candy” and “What Time Is It” among others. Rounding out the nominations this year were “Push It to the Limit” and “I Feel Love” writer Pete Bellotte, “No Scrubs” and “Bills Bills Bills” writer Kandi Burruss, “Song of the South” writer Bob McDill, The House That Built Me” writer Tom Douglas and “Black Pearl” and “Candida” writer Toni Wine.

Notably included in the non-performing songwriter list as well is the Black Eyed Peas’ Will.i.am, who along with writing his own group’s hits such as “Where is the Love” and “I’ve Got a Feeling,” has helped pen hits for others including John Legend’s “Ordinary People,” Britney Spears’ “Work Bitch” and Fergie’s “Glamorous.”

entertainment.title: From Ticketing To Vocals, The ‘Mind-Blowing’ Ways Concerts Are Using AI
entertainment.summary: Whether aiding in concert discovery or simply making shows sound a lot better, new AI tools are helping live thrive.
entertainment.body:
As Trent Reznor performed a dramatic piano rendition of Nine Inch Nails’ “Something I Can Never Have,” his voice ­resounded throughout the arena, crystal clear. Whether Reznor was singing an intimate B-stage number like this or NIN’s heavier dance and rock material, his vocals sounded crisper than ever before.

That’s because on this year’s Peel It Back Tour, the band’s front of house sound engineer, Jamie Pollock, had, for the first time, used L-Acoustics’ Source Intelligence. The pro audio company created the technology to utilize nongenerative machine learning to help identify an artist’s voice in real time — and deliver it to the crowd, free of any other background noises that a microphone might pick up onstage. Pollock kept his experiment “hush-hush” throughout the entire run, but fans noticed the difference.

“Trent’s whispering at times; he’s trying to make it as intimate as possible,” Pollock says. “And then [the next] minute, he’s screaming.”

As in most aspects of life now, AI continues to expand in the live-music space, whether it’s being deployed by long-established companies like L-Acoustics or newer AI power players like Suno. The latter hired Michael Chua, previously a Ticketmaster executive, as vp/GM of its new Suno Live Experiences division upon its launch in October.

Bad actors, too, have taken to using AI in the live sector. Scalpers are unleashing more bots than ever to help purchase tickets. In October, RAYE posted on Instagram that her show at London’s 5,000-­capacity Royal Albert Hall had received 1.8 million presale sign-ups. “Hundreds of thousands of fake registrations” had been recorded, she wrote. “It is a new world we are living in now, I have never witnessed bots on this scale.”

But by and large, AI is helping concerts and tours run smoother from end to end — and ­whether or not fans are aware, it’s integrated into more aspects of the scene than ever.

For as long as artists have been touring, marketers have been tasked with getting the word out — and AI is reshaping even this long-established aspect of the business. Companies such as Laylo and HIVE help artist teams send SMS and email campaigns, with Laylo often working directly with artists and HIVE frequently serving venues themselves.

According to Laylo, its clients include ­Sabrina Carpenter, Ariana Grande and Noah Kahan, who utilize the platform for tour announcements and SMS messages going out to fans who’ve opted in for sign-ups. Laylo also can link directly to Instagram, allowing for easy communication on social media. HIVE, meanwhile, works with clients including the major dance promoter Insomniac and provides similar services for SMS and email.

entertainment.title: Martin McDonagh to Receive Outstanding Achievement in Directing Award at Palm Springs International Film Festival (Exclusive)
entertainment.summary: The Film Awards will take place on Jan. 7, 2027, with the festival running from Jan. 7 to Jan. 18.
entertainment.body:
Wild Horse Nine writer and director Martin McDonagh will receive the Outstanding Achievement in Directing Award at the Palm Springs International Film Festival , the Palm Springs International Film Awards announced on Thursday.

The Film Awards will take place on Jan. 7, 2027, with the festival running from Jan. 7 to Jan. 18.

“Martin McDonagh remains one of our most distinctive and original voices in cinema today,” Festival Chairman Nachhattar Singh Chandi says. “Over the course of his celebrated career, he has built a body of work that is humorous, timely and morally complex. Wild Horse Nine is another testament to his singular vision, and we are honored to recognize him and his extraordinary film with the Outstanding Achievement in Directing Award.” Related Stories Movies Milcho Manchevski's 'Sister Brother Manhole Cover' Wins Top Prize at Tokyo Film Fest TV Tony Awards to Air on CBS Through 2032

Wild Horse Nine stars John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell as CIA agents who set out to Easter Island shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup to confront their dark pasts. Their trip gets turned upside down when they meet a pair of rebellious students, played by Mariana di Girolamo and Ailin Salas.

McDonagh is an award-winning filmmaker and playwright whose credits include In Bruges , Seven Psychopaths , Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri and The Banshees of Inisherin . For Three Billboards and Banshees , he received Oscar nominations for best picture, best director for Banshees , and best original screenplay for In Bruges , Three Billboards and Banshees . He has also won six BAFTAs and three Golden Globes.

McDonagh joins this year’s previously announced Vanguard Award recipient The Invite , with Seth Rogen, Olivia Wilde, Penelope Cruz and Edward Norton will collect. Past director award recipients include Jane Campion ( The Power of the Dog ), Alejandro G. Iñárritu ( Babel, Birdman ), Greta Gerwig ( Barbie ), Steve McQueen ( 12 Years a Slave ), Sarah Polley ( Women Talking ), David O. Russell ( The Fighter ), Quentin Tarantino ( Once Upon a Time in Hollywood ) and Chloé Zhao ( Nomadland ).

entertainment.body:
Ego Nwodim and Chabely Ponce are set to star in I’m With Stupid , a high school comedy directed by Hannah Pearl Utt ( Cora Bora ).

Upgrade is handling international sales on the project and will launch it to buyers at the upcoming American Film Market .

Written by Carolina Barlow ( The Hawk ) and Peter Kelly ( Big Mouth ), the film follows a pair of directionless high school seniors from opposite ends of the social spectrum who are forced to work together to avoid the humiliation of failing senior year. Related Stories Movies Sony Pictures Classics Takes Jean-Pierre Jeunet's 'Violette' for U.S. Movies Suzanne Farwell's Starry Rom-Com 'Otherwise Engaged' Sells Wide Ahead of AFM (Exclusive)

Tremblay ( Room , Wonder , Good Boys ) plays Noah, a senior with an opinion on everything but no motivation. Ponce ( Girl Group ) is Hadley, Noah’s wealthy classmate who discovers she may have interests beyond becoming a trophy wife.

McKinnon ( Barbie , Ghostbusters ) will portray Principal Dunlap, the school’s deeply unpopular and increasingly vindictive administrator. Nwodim ( Return to You , Hoppers ) is Ms. Reed, the students’ unconventional English teacher, who becomes an unlikely ally in their fight to graduate.

“I’m thrilled to make a movie that’s this funny but has this much heart, with my dream group of collaborators,” Utt said.

Mallory Schwartz ( The Morning Show, Cora Bora ) and Jen Goyne Blake ( Joyland ) are producing. Jonathan Kier and Matt Brodlie are executive producing for Upgrade, alongside Christine D’Souza for After Hours, Marc Danon and Kyle Fox for Fox Global Capital and April Shih for Diversity Hire.

“There’s a real appetite for smart, unapologetically funny comedies,” said Kier and Brodlie of Upgrade. “Hannah has a terrific ability to find genuine emotion in absurd situations, and with this exceptional ensemble, we believe I’m With Stupid has all the ingredients to become a new generation’s favorite high school comedy.”

Chris Pratt has been tapped to receive the King of Comedy Award at the 2026 Kids’ Choice Awards on Nov. 14.

The Guardians of the Galaxy and Parks and Recreation alum will receive the Silver Blimp statuette at the show, which is officially titled CBS Presents Nickelodeon Kids’ Choice Awards, in celebration of his career, “before facing Nickelodeon’s iconic slime,” according to the announcement. Pratt also might take home an Orange Blimp award that night as he is nominated for favorite male animated voice from a movie for his role as Mario in The Super Mario Galaxy Movie. Pratt next stars in Way of the Warrior Kid, an adaptation of Jocko Willink’s bestselling children’s novel that premieres Nov. 25 on Apple TV, which he also produced.

“I’m incredibly honored to receive Nickelodeon’s King of Comedy Award,” Pratt said. “I spent most of my childhood trying to make people laugh to get out of trouble. Now apparently you can win awards for it. Pretty sweet deal. Comedy has always been a huge part of my life, and making people laugh is one of my favorite things in the world. Especially kids. I’m grateful to Nickelodeon and CBS for this honor. And if I get slimed, just know I’ll be sending them my dry-cleaning bill.”

The 2026 KCAs will be hosted by Alex Warren . Musical performances and other celebrity appearances will be announced at a later date. Taylor Swift leads this year’s nominees with a total of six mentions, followed by Ariana Grande and Sabrina Carpenter with five apiece.

Awards will be handed out across film, television, music, gaming, sports and other categories. Among the movies and series that are up for KCAs are The Super Mario Galaxy Movie, Toy Story 5, Wednesday , Wicked: For Good , The SpongeBob Movie: Search for SquarePants, KPop Demon Hunters and Percy Jackson and the Olympians.
