entertainment.body:
Robert Pattinson is getting some special recognition after his very busy year.

The star will be honored as the 40th recipient of the American Cinematheque Award, presented at the organization’s Beverly Hills gala on Feb. 9. In 2026 alone, Pattinson has starred in The Drama , The Odyssey , Primetime and the upcoming Dune: Part Three , and the evening will celebrate those as well as his wide-ranging two-decade career.

“Rob has built an extraordinary career defined by his unwavering dedication to his craft, fearless creative choices, and remarkable versatility as an actor. From his collaborations with some of cinema’s most visionary filmmakers to his ability to captivate audiences in major studio blockbusters, Rob has continually challenged expectations and demonstrated the power of great storytelling,” American Cinematheque board chair Rick Nicita said in a statement. “Rob is the perfect choice to receive this award and join our esteemed list of artists who not only love cinema but continue to have a deep impact on our industry. We are thrilled that his filming schedule has allowed us the opportunity to recognize his exceptional contributions to film and we look forward to celebrating his continued achievements.” Related Stories Movies Scarlett Johansson Breaks Silence on 'The Batman Part II' Role: "It Was Very Hard to Figure Out" Lifestyle Jon Bernthal Adds Another Notch on Packed 2026 Résumé by Fronting Fear of God Campaign

Ryan Gosling was previously set to receive the American Cinematheque Award in a ceremony this month, but the event was rescheduled after Gosling was no longer available to accept it; Pattinson has also been busy this fall, filming The Batman Part II while taking part in the awards race.

The American Cinematheque Awards Gala serves as an annual fundraiser for the nonprofit, supporting its year-round programming at the Aero Theatre in Santa Monica, Los Feliz 3 Theatre in Los Feliz and Egyptian Theatre in Hollywood. The American Cinematheque Award has previously been given to stars including Eddie Murphy, Steven Spielberg, Martin Scorsese, Jodie Foster, Denzel Washington, Nicole Kidman, George Clooney and Michael B. Jordan.

entertainment.summary: From Netflix and Hulu to Apple TV and HBO Max, these phone plans can help TV and movie fans bundle their favorite streaming services to save on monthly bills.
entertainment.body:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, The Hollywood Reporter may receive an affiliate commission.

For viewers who always have another series queued up or a movie night planned, a cell phone plan that includes streaming subscriptions can help make the monthly entertainment budget go further. Wireless network providers like T-Mobile and Verizon offer options that pair wireless services with entertainment perks, whether that means access to a streaming platform or discounts on subscriptions.

Streaming bundles remain relatively uncommon in the wireless market, making them a valuable perk when choosing a phone carrier. If you’re already paying for a similar plan with another provider, opting for a carrier that includes streaming benefits is a no-brainer and can help you save on subscriptions you’d otherwise pay for separately. Jordan and Yerin Ha Front David Yurman's New York-Set Holiday Campaign

Networks like Spectrum do not include streaming apps directly with standalone mobile plans, as entertainment benefits are instead tied to Spectrum TV and internet packages. Mint Mobile also doesn’t bundle free streaming subscriptions with its phone plans, while AT&T’s current wireless plans don’t include streaming subscriptions either. Verizon offers a range of streaming subscriptions at discounted prices as add-ons, while T-Mobile stands out as a top option for customers looking for a wireless carrier that actually includes streaming subscriptions in their phone plans.

Starting Nov. 5, T-Mobile’s new T-Mix lets customers build a phone plan that fits their lifestyle while adding the entertainment perks they actually want. Across three plan tiers (Standard, More and Loaded), customers can customize their experience with Picks for streaming favorites like ESPN Unlimited, YouTube Premium, Hulu and Netflix. With up to four free Picks changes per year, customers can adjust their plan as their needs evolve.

For movie and TV fans, the right phone plan can offer more than reliable connectivity. Comparing included subscriptions, discounted add-ons and the services you already watch can help reveal whether bundling saves money or simply adds another perk to the monthly bill.

entertainment.title: Former UTA and FaZe Clan Execs Launch Creator Management Firm ISO
entertainment.summary: Mike Lee, the former head of gaming and livestreaming at UTA Creators, and Darren Yan, former chief talent officer at FaZe Clan, are launching the firm, which is backed by Influence Media Partners.
entertainment.body:
A pair of veteran executives from the creator space are launching new venture meant to help digital creators expand their businesses across content, music, products and live experiences.

The management and representation company is called ISO, and is being launched by Mike Lee, the former head of gaming and livestreaming at UTA Creators, who is CEO, and Darren Yan, former chief talent officer at FaZe Clan, who is head of music.

ISO is backed by Influence Media Partners, the music and entertainment-focused investment company.

The company’s talent roster includes PlaqueBoyMax, Jasontheween, Ironmouse, Lacy, Vanillamace, Kyedae, RDCWorld, with brand clients that include Electronic Arts, Discord, Underdog and Icenova. ISO says it has more than 90 clients, with a heavy focus on livestreamers, gamers, artists, VTubers and lifestyle creators across beauty, food and other verticals.

Creators are increasingly leveraging the audiences they have built through their streams and social channels to build businesses elsewhere, and at the same time brands are eager to work with creators on campaigns and original content. Firms like ISO can help connect those dots.

“The next household name is already online, building an audience, and ISO was built for that talent,” said Mike Lee, CEO and co-founder of ISO. “Today’s gatekeepers are algorithms, so understanding discovery, engagement and how content travels is essential. Every creator we work with is running a real business, and our job is to give it room to grow through original IP, products, live events, and expansion into China and platforms like TikTok Shop, where most of the industry still isn’t set up to compete.”

“At Influence, we look to invest in partners who bring an innovative approach to the business of culture and entertainment,” added Lylette Pizarro, founder & co-managing partner of Influence Media Partners. “Mike, Darren and the team at ISO are reimagining talent representation for a creator economy that has fundamentally transformed how audiences are built, culture is shaped and revenue is generated. ISO’s playbook directly aligns with our values and investment philosophy, and we’re excited to support their growth.”

“Talent development used to be the heart of every company in the representation business. ISO is bringing it back with our model built for the new generation where musicians and creators increasingly share the same playbook: build an audience directly, then build a business around it,” said Darren Yan, co-founder and head of music at ISO. “We invest in our clients from the earliest stages across music, media, products, live events, gaming and tech, with our A&R team applying the same lens to artists by building global fandom online before the market catches on.”

entertainment.title: Sony Pictures Classics Takes Jean-Pierre Jeunet’s ‘Violette’ for U.S.
entertainment.summary: SPC, which released Jeunet's 'Amelie,' 'Micmacs' and 'The City of Lost Children,' will also release his new feature in Latin America and Southeast Asia.
entertainment.body:
Sony Pictures Classics has snapped up all rights in the United States, Latin America and Southeast Asia to Violette , the new film from Amelie director Jean-Pierre Jeunet.

The French drama, based on Valérie Perrin’s international bestseller Fresh Water for Flowers , the film follows Violette, a cemetery caretaker — played by Once Upon My Mother actress Leïla Bekhti — whose peaceful life is disrupted with the arrival of a mysterious stranger (Melvil Poupaud) who insists on depositing the ashes of his recently departed mother on the gravesite of a complete stranger. His arrival will force Violette to confront hidden truths of her troubled past filled with hidden truths. Matthias Schoenaerts ( Rust and Bone , The Danish Girl ) co-stars.

Violette marks SPC’s fourth collaboration with Jeunet, following the releases of Amelie (2001), Micmacs (2009) and The City of Lost Children (1995).

“Jean-Pierre Jeunet has a singular gift for weaving together multiple storylines with humor, pathos and that unmistakable touch of whimsy,” SPC said in a statement. “We’re especially delighted that Violette marks our fourth film together. It continues his lyrical tradition while also feeling completely fresh, and theatrical audiences will be enchanted.”

SPC did not reveal details of their planned rollout for the film. The was negotiated between Sony Pictures Classics and Studiocanal, who are handling international sales.
